subject: MAP: unit-econ / tokens-per-$ sanity check + batching/cache questions
messages:
From: Tom Reynolds <tom@pulsewavehealth.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>, procurement@pulsewavehealth.com
Date: 2029-05-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MAP ask - unit econ verification and preftech/batching assumptions

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. As we start to lock down the MAP timeline with Procurement, they want a short, documented validation of the unit economics assumptions that underpin the SOW: tokens per transaction, expected hit rates for prefix/KV cache, and recommended batching settings for our busiest endpoints (clinical note generation and patient triage).

Attached is the MAP draft — you'll see our internal traffic model + expected p95 response length. Two quick asks:
- Can you confirm tokens-per-response assumptions and a realistic tokens/$ estimate for the hosted plan vs dedicated?
- What caching hit-rate should we model for prefetch vs prefix caching? We need a conservative and a best-case number for the MAP (and ideally a suggested experiment to prove it).

Procurement is pushing for a close by 6/14 so we can start onboarding in Q3. If you can flag any gating questions we should add to the MAP, that helps.

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Reynolds
Director, Product @ PulseWave Health
[Attachment: pulsewave_map_unit_econ.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom@pulsewavehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-05-20T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP ask - unit econ verification and preftech/batching assumptions

Tom — thanks, this is exactly the right time to freeze those items into the MAP. I skimmed the attachment and pulled a couple immediate notes:

- Tokens per response: under your sample prompts p50 ~850 tokens, p95 ~1,700 tokens. We'll run an eval pass to sanity-check rounding and streaming overhead, but those ballpark numbers look right.
- Tokens/$: hosted (standard model catalog selection) we estimate $0.0019 per token-equivalent at current pricing profiles; dedicated will vary by commit but ballpark ~30–45% lower depending on GPU family and batch shape. I'll have Ben pull more precise numbers and a delta table.
- Caching: conservative prefix-cache hit for the first 2 weeks of live traffic = 5–10%; stable state best-case ~25–35% for predictable prompts. For KV prefetch (session affinities), conservative 2–6% -> best-case 18–25% depending on user flow. We'll include both conservative / expected ranges in the MAP.

Ben, Vivek — can you add two things: (1) a short spreadsheet tab with tokens-per-call by endpoint (sample prompt and streaming overhead) and (2) a recommended small-scale experiment (1-week canary) to measure prefix-hit and KV-hit rates under production routing?

Tom — proposed next steps and timeline inside the MAP draft:
- 5/21: Redwood posts a short unit-econ appendix with conservative vs expected numbers (I can get a draft by EOD)
- 5/24-5/30: canary eval (1 week) to measure cache hit-rate and per-call token distribution
- 6/05: MAP updated + mutual signoff of assumptions
- 6/14: procurement close target

If procurement needs more headroom on the timeline, flag and we can extend the MAP.

—Grace
Grace O'Connor
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>

Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-05-21T09:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP ask - unit econ verification and preftech/batching assumptions

Grace wrote:
> Ben, Vivek — can you add two things: (1) a short spreadsheet tab with tokens-per-call by endpoint (sample prompt and streaming overhead) and (2) a recommended small-scale experiment (1-week canary) to measure prefix-hit and KV-hit rates under production routing?

Attaching the initial tab (pulsewave_map_unit_econ.xlsx). Notes below; I've kept the language non-technical for Procurement but included an ops section for the SRE/Eng owners.

Quick technical assumptions (summary):
- Measurement method: we recommend instrumenting token counts at ingress + egress with sampling at 1% to get distribution. Sampling reduces cost while preserving tail estimates.
- Tokens per logical transaction: clinical-note-draft = median 820 / p95 1,640. triage-summary = median 420 / p95 950. We included 6% streaming overhead in the spreadsheet (prompt framing + JSON wrapper).
- Batching: for latency-sensitive routes we recommend max batch windows of 12–25ms with dynamic batch sizing; this gives 5–22% cost savings in our sims depending on QPS shape. Spreadsheet has the batch-sim tab.
- Caching: prefix caching assumptions use conservative (5%), expected (20%), optimistic (35%). For KV/session cache we propose a canary with sticky sessions for 10% of traffic to estimate warm cache hit.

Proposed canary plan (high level):
1) 5/24–5/30: route 5–10% of production traffic via a Redwood canary pool with caching enabled + sampling of token telemetry.
2) Daily sync: short readout email with p50/p95 token distribution and prefix/KV hit rates.
3) Deliverable: delta to MAP token/$ and recommended commit level for Dedicated vs Hosted by 6/05.

Operational asks for PulseWave:
- Confirm the two endpoints we should instrument (clinical-note-draft, triage-summary) and a test tenant to route 5% of traffic.
- Point us to an SRE contact for firewall/VPC if you want the canary in your VPC.

Tom — attaching the spreadsheet and a quick CSV that contains the sim inputs (sizing-assumptions.csv).

Regards,
Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

- Procurement asked for an explicit conservative pricing delta if we miss the canary targets (i.e., if the observed cache hits are below conservative thresholds). Can Redwood draft a fallback pricing clause we can include in the MAP addendum? (simple: 90-day review + unit price ladder if cache < 8% over the canary).

Agree with the timeline you proposed — 6/05 signoff on assumptions is workable. If you can circulate the unit-econ appendix and the canary runbook today/tomorrow that will let Procurement start their internal review.

Tom
